facts.statement: The genus Eoalulavis was named by Sanz and colleagues in 1996.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Sanz et al., 1996

facts.statement: Eoalulavis lived during the Barremian stage of the Lower Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived during the Barremian, in the Lower Cretaceous around 125 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Eoalulavis were found at the Las Hoyas Konservat-Lagerstätte in Cuenca, Spain.
facts.quote: Its remains came from the Konservat-Lagerstätte of Las Hoyas, Cuenca, Spain

facts.statement: The fossil preserves body remains, primary and secondary feathers, and a bastard wing covered in limonite.
facts.quote: It also preserves remains of the body, primary, secondary feathers and a bastard wing which have been covered by layers of limonite as a result of the fossilization process

facts.statement: Eoalulavis was roughly the size of a European goldfinch, with bony wing elements measuring about 17 centimeters.
facts.quote: E. hoyasi was roughly the size of a european goldfinch (Carduelis carduelis), with the bony elements of its wings approximately 17 centimeters (7 inches) in length

facts.statement: Later studies estimated the bird weighed approximately 45 grams with a total wingspan of about 26 centimeters.
facts.quote: Later studies estimated that it had a weight of approximately 45 grams (1.6 ounces) and total wingspan (including feathers) of about 26 centimeters (10 inches)

facts.statement: Some researchers describe the unique shape of the Eoalulavis sternum as "spear-shaped" or "fish-shaped".
facts.quote: This form has been described as "spear-shaped" or "fish-shaped" by some

facts.statement: The forelimb morphology includes large ungual phalanges on the alular and major digits, with the minor digit bearing two phalanges.
facts.quote: The alular and major digits both bear a large ungual phalanx and the minor one bears two phalanx

facts.statement: At the time of its discovery, Eoalulavis was the earliest known bird to possess an alula, a structure used for flight stability.
facts.quote: At the time of its discovery, it was the earliest bird known to possess an alula, a batch of feathers on the alular (first) digit that in modern birds can be separately moved to improve stability at low flight speeds

facts.statement: Research indicates Eoalulavis could perform continuous flapping flight but was likely unable to glide due to its body mass.
facts.quote: The study also found that they were capable of continuous flapping flight, but were likely unable to glide due to having a high body mass to wingspan ratio

facts.statement: The holotype preserves crustacean cuticles in the abdomen area, interpreted as the bird's last meal.
facts.quote: The holotype preserves concentrated remains of crustacean cuticles in the area of the abdomen, interpreted as its last meal

facts.statement: This fossil provided the first direct evidence of feeding behavior in Enantiornithes and Mesozoic birds.
facts.quote: It provided the first direct evidence of feeding behaviour in Enantiornithes and in Mesozoic birds in general

facts.statement: Researchers interpret the diet evidence as suggesting Eoalulavis lived in shorelines seeking invertebrates like modern turnstones.
facts.quote: This fact has been interpreted as evidence of an ecological role in Eoalulavis similar to that of extant waders; living mainly in the shore seeking for little invertebrates in a similar way of modern turnstones

facts.statement: The Las Hoyas locality was a seasonal subtropical wetland dominated by aquatic organisms during the Barremian.
facts.quote: The locality of Las Hoyas was in the Barremian a seasonal subtropical wetland ecologically dominated by fully aquatic organisms (e.g.: holostean fishes)

facts.statement: Eoalulavis is believed to have been the most adapted to a semi-aquatic environment among the local avifauna.
facts.quote: Eoalulavis hoyasi is believed to be the most linked to a semi-aquatic environment of the three

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses group Eoalulavis with the genus Liaoningornis as a derived group of Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: In the last cladistic analysis Eoalulavis groups with the Chinese genus Liaoningornis forming a monophyletic group of derived Enantiornithes

facts.statement: Eoalulavis is classified within Enantiornithes based on traits like a groove in the radius or a foramen in the coracoids.
facts.quote: These traits include a groove in the inter-osseous surface of radius or a conspicuous foramen in the dorsal surface of the strut-like coracoids

facts.statement: Only one species, Eoalulavis hoyasi, is currently known within this genus.
facts.quote: Sólo se conoce una especie, Eoalulavis hoyasi

facts.statement: Eoalulavis hoyasi was the size of a modern goldfinch with a wingspan of about 17 centimeters.
facts.quote: Eoalulavis hoyasi tenía el tamaño de un jilguero moderno, con unos 17 centímetros de envergadura (distancia de extremo a extremo de las alas extendidas)

facts.statement: Upon discovery, Eoalulavis was the oldest known bird to possess an alula, a feather structure acting as a high-lift device.
facts.quote: En el momento de su descubrimiento, fue la más antigua ave en disponer de un álula, un conjunto de plumas en el pulgar que puede moverse por separado para actuar como un dispositivo hipersustentador

facts.statement: The holotype shows crustacean exoskeleton remains in the thoracic cavity, interpreted as fossilized stomach contents.
facts.quote: El holotipo presenta restos del exoesqueleto de crustáceos en su cavidad torácica que han sido interpretados como evidencias fosilizadas del contenido estomacal del animal

facts.statement: The fossil record for Eoalulavis spans from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)
